sentences.text: This gate reads all six attributes. It acts on 143 of 345 training cases, none of which is actually 'yes'; for the typical case it acts on (every attribute at its first value), it takes the predicted probability of 'yes' from above 99% without it to below 1% with it.

How much one attribute matters depends on the others: for the typical case, moving a5 away from 1 takes the predicted probability of 'yes' from below 1% to about 84% when a3 = 2, and a3 = 2 instead of 1 takes it to about 75% when a6 = 2, while with a3 = 1 or a6 = 1 it stays below 1%.

Through it, a3 = 2 raises the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes' to about 1%, and a5 other than 1, a6 = 2 and a1 other than 1 also raise it, while giving a2 or a4 its first value lowers it, all below 1% otherwise.

This ramp adds up all six attributes with fixed weights. Through it, giving a2 or a4 its first value and a4 = 3 instead of 2 raise the typical case's predicted probability of 'yes', and moving a1, a3, a6 or a5 away from its first value lowers it, though it stays below 1%.

The model predicts 'yes' when exactly two of a1 to a6 take their first value, and otherwise not: at every count, all the training cases get the same prediction, and the average training case with two attributes at their first value gets about 82%, against about 4% for the other counts.
One small unit on a2 never switches on and does not change the predictions.

parts.name: exactly_two_of_six
parts.original_hypothesis: The output composes the three children additively under a final ReLU: score = ReLU(2.716 + Ramp - 7.339*Gate - 2.874*Inert), with Inert identically zero. The ramp crosses the decision boundary between one and two active rule indicators, forming the lower edge of a response peak; when a third indicator activates, the gate fires and its -7.34-weighted readout overwhelms the ramp's rise, forming the upper edge. The model therefore scores positive exactly when two of the six indicators are active: a peak at count two realised by one linear ramp plus a single at-least-three gate under the output threshold - more parsimonious than the textbook two-gate bump construction. Extensionally equal to the MONK-2 rule (exactly two of {a1=1..a6=1}) on all 432 possible inputs.

parts.name: count_gate_atleast3
parts.original_hypothesis: An at-least-three-of-six detector. The unit aggregates the six MONK-2 rule indicators (attribute takes its first value): a1:1, a2:1, a4:1, a5:1 enter directly with positive weights; the binary attributes a3 and a6 enter via their complements a3:2, a6:2 with strongly negative weights, which is the same signal inverted. In indicator terms the pre-activation is a near-uniform weighted count (per-indicator coefficients 4.49 to 7.07) minus 14.86: the largest possible two-indicator sum leaves it at -1.82 (off), the smallest possible three-indicator sum reaches +1.26 (on). The unit therefore fires if and only if at least three of the six rule indicators are active, over all 64 indicator patterns.

parts.name: linear_count_ramp
parts.original_hypothesis: A linear count ramp. Evaluated per attribute, the direct connections contribute a positive amount when the attribute takes its first value (a1 +2.56, a2 +2.73, a3 +1.93, a4 +1.69, a5 +2.63, a6 +1.91) and a negative amount otherwise (between -0.02 and -2.03, with small within-attribute variation, e.g. a1=2 vs a1=3 differ by 0.18). The sum therefore rises approximately linearly with the number of active rule indicators; together with the output bias, it crosses zero between one and two active indicators, forming the lower edge of the model's response peak.

closed_form.rounding: weights and biases at 3 significant figures

parts.name: inert_unit_a23
parts.original_hypothesis: An inert unit. The node computes ReLU(0.443 * z(a2:3) - 1.118), and z(a2:3) takes only two values (approximately -0.72 and +1.39), giving maximum pre-activation approximately -0.50 < 0. The unit therefore outputs exactly zero on every input in the domain, and its -2.87 readout to the output contributes nothing. Structurally present, functionally absent: unearned structure that survived selection because nothing priced it.

closed_form.rounding: weights and biases at 3 significant figures

parts.name: pruned_inputs
parts.original_hypothesis: Feature exclusion by elimination. Inputs a2:2 and a4:3 carry no enabled connections: deletion mutations severed them and selection never restored them. The model provably does not consult these features - their values cannot influence any node. For the MONK-2 rule both are redundant given their siblings: a2:2 is implied by a2:1 and a2:3 under one-hot encoding, and a4:3 by a4:1 and a4:2.

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording
